references.text: The Lord scattered them over the whole earth – exactly what they feared in verse 4 ('so that we will not be scattered over the face of the whole earth').
Cities that are great and fortified up to heaven – the same expression ('with its top in the heavens') used concerning the Tower of Babel.
The king of Babylon says: 'I will ascend to heaven' – parallel to the Tower of Babel where people wanted to build a tower with its top in the heavens.
The nations rage and plot against the Lord and his anointed – parallel to humanity's collective rebellion against God's will at Babel.
Babylon the great has fallen – the final judgment on human pride and rebellion against God, with roots tracing back to the Tower of Babel.
David made a name for himself – the same expression as in Gen 11:4 ('let us make a name for ourselves'), but here it is God who gives glory.
Contrast between tower-building for one's own glory (Babel) and city-building after seeking God (Judah).
Fundamental contrast between God's creation ('Let us') and human rebellion ('Let us').
Theological contrast: humanity's perishable city (Babel) versus God's eternal city (Heaven).
Contrast in 'making a name': through God's blessing (Ruth) versus human rebellion (Babel).
